newsitem.title: FRANCE: PARIS BOURSE ENDS HIGHER AFTER STORM BREAK.
newsitem.headline: PARIS BOURSE ENDS HIGHER AFTER STORM BREAK.

text.p: French shares closed higher on Wednesday but off the day's highs after a late interruption in trade caused by a storm.
* CAC-40 index finished up 32.01 points, or 1.2 percent, at 2,696.19 after a late fixing around 1520 GMT.
* CAC-40 Jun futures 2,683 vs 2,688 at Wednesdays close.
Brokers said the disruption to the quote system that occurred 20 minutes before the close had little impact on the direction of the bourse, which was tracking Wall Street's moves.

* Renault recouped most of the previous day's 4.63 percent loss, closing up 4.07 percent at 133 francs. The company's announcement that it had commissioned an independent study on alternatives to the proposed closure of the Vilvoorde plant was perceived by the market as a political compromise that was unlikely to derail its restructuring plans.
"The plant's survival chances are minimal," one investment analyst said. But another said the stock would be volatile until all uncertainty were removed.
* Car parts supplier Valeo, whose restructuring effort has been praised by the government for its more conciliatory style, closed up 3.54 percent at 357 francs.
* Schneider rose 3.57 percent to 315.90 francs after forecasting a significant improvement in its 1997 results at the annual general meeting on Tuesday.
* Carrefour, a favourite among foreign investors, closed up 3.44 percent at 4,034 francs.
* Privatisation stocks Lagardere and Thomson-CSF continue to underperform. Lagardere was unchanged. Thomson-CSF fell 0.77 percent.
* The dollar's weakness weighed on oil majors Elf Aquitaine, down 0.63 percent, and Total, down 1.07 percent.
